name: Diffusion models

conventions.text: Draw the denoising network as a bow-tie: two triangles or trapezoids meeting at a narrow waist (narrowing encoder, widening decoder), left empty or holding bars that shrink and then grow, instead of a plain labelled box.
Depict noise as a picture: a square of pixel noise as the generator's starting input, or as the predicted noise at the output end.
Mark training state by fill colour plus an icon: the frozen pretrained model in one fill with a small padlock or snowflake on it, the part being trained in a contrasting warm yellow.
Bring the timestep t and the condition (class label y, or c) in at the bottom as their own small labelled inputs beside the image input.
Draw conditioning as one line running alongside the network with short arrow taps dropping into each layer it modulates, rather than a separate arrow per layer from the source.

For a backbone figure, stack the layers bottom-to-top in a narrow column (noised input at the base, predicted noise or output at the top) and draw the repeated block's internals in a tall rounded panel to the right of the stack.
Draw residual and long skip paths as thick black elbow lines down one side of the stack, merging through a circled glyph (+ or C).
Tie a detail panel to the element it expands by repeating that element's colour on the panel (its fill tint, its outline, or a border and title tab in the trained part's colour).

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
